Three-Panel Effect-Distribution Violin from Simulation Results

Source: R/plot_effect_distribution.R
plot_effect_distribution.Rd

Builds a three-panel violin plot (ITT / identified \(\hat H\) / identified \(\hat H^c\)) of treatment-effect estimates across simulation replicates produced by run_simulation_analysis(). Handles both GLM endpoints (OR, RD, IRR) and survival (HR), optionally inverts effects to a benefit scale (subgroup_notation = "benefit"), and overlays a dotted reference line at the DGM-implied true effect in \(\hat H\).

Usage

plot_effect_distribution(
  results,
  analysis_method = "FS",
  effect_measure = c("OR", "HR", "RD", "IRR", "MD"),
  subgroup_notation = c("harm", "benefit"),
  reference_effect = NA_real_,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  panel_labels = NULL,
  drop_undetected = TRUE,
  trim_threshold = 1000,
  trim_fraction = 0.01,
  ylim = NULL
)

Arguments

results

data.frame returned by run_simulation_analysis() (optionally filtered). Must contain the columns analysis, any.H, hr.itt, hr.H.hat, and hr.Hc.hat. The column names end in .hr regardless of the underlying effect measure (OR / HR / RD / IRR); this follows the package's established naming convention.

analysis_method

Character. Method label in the analysis column to plot (e.g. "FS", "GRF"). Default: "FS".

effect_measure

Character. One of "OR", "HR", "RD", "IRR", "MD". Used only for axis labelling and to decide the y-axis reference line (\(1\) for ratio measures, \(0\) for risk / mean differences). "MD" (mean difference) is treated additively like "RD". Default: "OR".

subgroup_notation

Character. "harm" leaves effects on the original (switched) scale; "benefit" inverts multiplicative effects via \(1/\hat\theta\) and flips the sign of additive effects so that larger values favour the benefit subgroup. Default: "harm".

reference_effect

Numeric or NA. Optional overlay showing the DGM-implied true effect in \(\hat H\) (e.g. 1 / dgm$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup on a benefit scale). Drawn as a dotted darkgreen line. Default: NA.

title

Character. Plot title. Default: auto-constructed.

subtitle

Character or NULL. Plot subtitle. Default: NULL.

panel_labels

Named character vector with names "itt", "H", "Hc" and the display labels for each violin. Default: c(itt = "ITT", H = "Identified H-hat", Hc = "Identified Hc-hat"). When subgroup_notation = "benefit", the default Hc label is adjusted to "Identified Hc-hat (benefit)".

drop_undetected

Logical. Restrict the \(\hat H\) and \(\hat H^c\) panels to replicates where a subgroup was identified (any.H == 1). Default: TRUE. The ITT panel always uses all replicates.

trim_threshold

Numeric or NULL. Trimming is applied only if any of the three groups has a raw mean exceeding this absolute value – i.e., extreme outliers that distort the violin or push annotated mean/SD into scientific notation. Default: 1000, matching build_estimation_table so the plot and the companion gt table auto-trim on the same condition. Set NULL to disable trimming entirely; set a smaller value (e.g., 100) to be more aggressive on plots where reasonable OR / HR / IRR estimates sit well below 100 and even moderate outliers visibly distort the violin axis.

trim_fraction

Numeric in (0, 0.5). Fraction of observations to trim from each tail of each group when trimming triggers. Default: 0.01 (1\ of values per group is kept). Has no effect when trim_threshold = NULL.

ylim

Numeric vector of length 2 or NULL. Explicit y-axis limits as c(lower, upper) applied via coord_cartesian (data are not dropped, only the viewport is clipped). Useful when extreme outlier estimates stretch the axis beyond the interesting range — e.g., ylim = c(0, 4) for OR benefit-scale plots. When NULL (default), limits are determined automatically by ggplot2.

Value

A ggplot2 object. Has attr(p, "panel_data") set to the long-format data.table used for plotting (for downstream summaries or diagnostic inspection). When trimming is active, also has attr(p, "trim_info") containing per-group diagnostics (n_total, n_trimmed, n_flagged, raw_mean, raw_sd, trimmed_mean, trimmed_sd, lower_bound, upper_bound).

Details

The MRCT analogue is SGplot_estimates, which works on the four-panel mrct_region_sims() schema (ITT / training / testing / subgroup). This function targets the three-panel run_simulation_analysis() schema that does not involve a train/test split.

See also

run_simulation_analysis for the simulation pipeline, SGplot_estimates for the MRCT analogue, build_estimation_table for the tabular counterpart.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Binary endpoint, benefit search, OR scale
true_or_benefit <- 1 / dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup
p <- plot_effect_distribution(
  results_alt,
  analysis_method   = "FS",
  effect_measure    = "OR",
  subgroup_notation = "benefit",
  reference_effect  = true_or_benefit,
  title             = "ACTG175 Binary (HTE): OR Estimates Across Simulations",
  subtitle          = sprintf("n = 1000, 50 sims | truth OR(Q) = %.2f",
                              true_or_benefit)
)
print(p)

# Survival endpoint, harm search, HR scale (no inversion)
p_surv <- plot_effect_distribution(
  results_alt,
  effect_measure    = "HR",
  subgroup_notation = "harm",
  reference_effect  = dgm_alt$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup
)

# Clip y-axis to focus on the interesting OR range
p_clipped <- plot_effect_distribution(
  results_alt,
  effect_measure    = "OR",
  subgroup_notation = "benefit",
  reference_effect  = true_or_benefit,
  ylim              = c(0, 4)
)
} # }
